w10_P4_002042: A laboratory shaker drives a mass of 5 kg on its table. That mass's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 9 times the value, plus 20, equals exactly 0. Two identical shakers are bolted to each bench, and 9 benches run at once, so the floor takes 9 times the force of a single bench pair. The floor log then adds 15 N for the frame preload and subtracts 28 N for the isolator reaction. What does the floor log record, in N?
w10_P4_002054: A fairground's season total is twice its month total, and the month total is 9 times a day's figure. A day's figure covers 3 identical rides, so it is 3 times the energy of a single car. A car has a mass of 4 kg on the scale model used for the estimate. The car's speed, in metres per second, is 14 more than the number of different pairs that can be chosen from the ride's 11 anchor posts, taking 2 at a time. What is the fairground's season total, in J?
w10_P4_002057: A cement works receives 258 sacks of one grade and 98 of another, and it stacks them in identical layers using the largest layer size that divides both counts exactly. A test trolley of mass 57 kg then runs at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that layer size. The works' balance takes the driving force in kilonewtons and subtracts 8 kN allowed for the rail anchors. Two trolleys run on each track, and the works has 12 identical tracks. The works' kiln fan is rated at 30 kW. What total does the works' balance give, in kN?
w10_P4_002059: A paper mill's hall figure adds 30 N for the frame preload and then a further 7 N for the load-pin offset to a bank total. The bank total is 9 times a rack's force, and a rack carries 8 identical drives pushing together. One drive moves a roll of mass 119 kg at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, equal to 3 times the sum of the two feed-dial readings, which are 5 and 13. The mill's dryer hood is 20 m long. What is the mill's hall figure, in N?
w10_P4_002061: A crane trolley of mass 136000 g runs along a gantry beam. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 3 times a number x, where x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 10 times x, plus 21, equals exactly 0. The gantry beam spans 24 m. The site sheet takes the driving force in kilonewtons, subtracts 19 kN allowed for the beam's own restraint, and then adds 18 kN for the tie-down anchors. What does the site sheet give, in kN?
w10_P4_002066: A packing plant tests a carton of mass 22 kg on a gravity chute. The carton's speed at the bottom, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 5 times the value, plus 4, equals exactly 0. Eight cartons run on each chute, 6 chutes serve every bay, and the plant operates 3 identical bays. How much energy do all the plant's cartons carry at once, in kJ?
w10_P4_002071: A cable-laying barge's log ends with an energy figure in kilojoules plus 11 kJ drawn by the winch house. Before that, the log doubles a single drum's net figure, because the barge works two identical drums. A drum's net figure is the carrier's kinetic energy less 29 J absorbed by the fairlead. The carrier has a mass of 14000 g, and its distance along the chute, in metres, is 2 times the cube of the elapsed seconds minus 2 times the square of the elapsed seconds. The log uses how fast the carrier is moving at the instant 2 seconds after release. What does the log end with, in kJ?
w10_P4_002073: A press shop meters its flywheel drive through a cycle, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 1 times t squared plus 8 times t. The ram's speed, in metres per second, equals the total that meter accumulates between the 3rd and the 4th second. The ram has a mass of 49000 g, and the shop's extraction duct is 16 m long. Four identical presses run together, so the shop total is 4 times one ram's energy. The shop's log then subtracts 3 J for the clutch and a further 7 J for the brake. What does the shop's log record, in J?
w10_P4_002079: A cable-car station's report is the frame force in kilonewtons, less 12 kN allowed for the tower's own restraint. The frame force is 7 times the force driving a single carrier, because 7 identical carriers hang from the same frame. A carrier has a mass of 96 kg. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 11 times the value, plus 28, equals exactly 0. What does the station's report give, in kN?
w10_P4_002082: A model-glider club launches a glider of mass 5000 g from a bungee line. The glider's distance along the launch line, in metres, is 3 times the cube of the elapsed seconds plus 0 times the square of the elapsed seconds, and the club uses how fast it is moving at the instant 1 second after release. The club's energy sheet takes the glider's kinetic energy in kilojoules and subtracts 16 kJ drawn by the winch. Six identical launches are made in a session, so the session figure is 6 times the single-launch figure. The club then subtracts a further 28 kJ for the field generator. What does the club's sheet end with, in kJ?
w10_P4_002083: A cargo lift's summary is the hoist force in kilonewtons plus 16 kN allowed for the car's own frame. The car carries a load of mass 23000 g in the test rig. That load's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is a meter total plus 27. The meter total is what the rig's gauge accumulates between the 0th and the 1st second, where the gauge's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 1 times t squared plus 5 times t. What is the lift's summary, in kN?
w10_P4_002084: A fairground test bench launches a car of mass 37000 g along a level rail. The car's speed, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 11 times the value, plus 28, equals exactly 0. Twelve identical cars are launched in a cycle, and the cycle sheet then subtracts 28 J absorbed by the catcher. The bench runs 3 identical cycles in a session. How much energy does a session account for, in J?
w10_P4_002085: A steel erector's site figure is a frame total plus 2 kN for the base plates. The frame total is 9 times a bank's force, and a bank is 11 identical jacks pushing together, each measured in kilonewtons. One jack drives a mass of 100 kg. That mass's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 4 times the value, plus 3, equals exactly 0. The site's tower crane reaches 45 m. What is the erector's site figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002093: A test track runs a sled of mass 28 kg along a level rail. The sled's distance from the start, in metres, is 4 times the cube of the elapsed seconds minus 1 times the square of the elapsed seconds, and the track uses how fast it is moving at the instant 2 seconds in. The track's floodlight draws 500 W. Five identical sleds run in each session, and the track holds 7 sessions in a day. How much energy do all of a day's runs account for, in kJ?
w10_P4_002094: A robotics bench drives a slide of mass 7000 g. The slide's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 8 times the value, plus 12, equals exactly 0. The bench's controller draws 65 W. The bench's balance sheet takes the driving force in kilonewtons, subtracts 1 kN for the mounting rail, then 15 kN for the granite base, and finally 19 kN for the anti-vibration mounts. What does the balance sheet give, in kN?
w10_P4_002102: A dockyard rig drives a carriage of mass 87000 g along its rails. The carriage's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 10 times the value, plus 16, equals exactly 0. Four identical carriages are pulled by each frame, so a frame takes 4 times the single-carriage force in kilonewtons, and the frame sheet then adds 11 kN for the rail clamps. The dockyard operates 4 identical frames. The dockyard's floodlight mast is 18 m tall. What total does the dockyard's sheet give, in kN?
w10_P4_002104: A joinery receives 219 dowels of one length and 276 of another, and it bundles them into identical packs using the largest pack size that divides both counts exactly. A test carriage of mass 49000 g is then driven at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, equal to 11 times that pack size. The workshop log takes the driving force and adds 4 N for the guide-rail drag. Nine identical carriages run on the same frame, and the log reports 9 times the single-carriage figure. The workshop's dust extractor is rated at 3 kW. What does the log report, in kN?
w10_P4_002113: A university lab receives 29 rods of one alloy and 251 of another, and it groups them into identical racks using the largest rack size that divides both counts exactly. A bench glider of mass 19 kg then moves at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that rack size. The lab's fume hood draws 350 W. The bench sheet takes the glider's kinetic energy, subtracts 22 J drawn by the blower, adds 24 J credited to the sensor supply, and then adds a further 15 J for the timer. What does the bench sheet total, in kJ?
w10_P4_002115: A conveyor plant's floor report is a hall force in kilonewtons, less 9 kN allowed for the building's own restraint. The hall force covers 7 identical banks, and each bank has 6 identical pushers working together. One pusher drives a tray of mass 40000 g. The tray's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is found by adding together all the whole numbers from 1 to 5, which are the plant's five speed-step numbers. What does the floor report give, in kN?
w10_P4_002116: A survey rig drives a mass of 57 kg on its sled. The sled's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is numerically equal to the number of different groups of 4 that can be chosen from the rig's 8 anchor points. Four identical sleds share a frame, and four identical frames make up the rig. The rig's beacon draws 45 W. The rig's log then subtracts 17 N for the load-cell offset. What does the log record, in kN?
w10_P4_002124: A bowling alley's test bench rolls a ball of mass 19 kg down the lane. The ball's speed, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 9 times the value, plus 18, equals exactly 0. The alley runs 10 identical lanes at once, so its floor total is 10 times the energy of a single ball. Expressed in kilojoules, the alley's sheet then adds 16 kJ drawn by the pinsetters. What does the alley's sheet give, in kJ?
w10_P4_002129: A theme park's water ride meters its pump through a surge, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 2 times t squared plus 8 times t. A boat's speed, in metres per second, equals the total that meter accumulates between the 2nd and the 3rd second. The boat has a mass of 12000 g on the scale model used for the estimate, and the ride's queue canopy is 40 m long. Nine boats run at once, and the ride sheet then subtracts 5 J absorbed by the brake pads. Expressed in kilojoules, the park's total then adds 19 kJ drawn by the pump house. What is the park's total, in kJ?
w10_P4_002131: A parcel hub's regional figure is 8 times a depot's figure, expressed in kilojoules. A depot's figure covers 12 identical chutes, and each chute handles 5 parcels at a time. One parcel has a mass of 13000 g. Its speed, in metres per second, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 4 times the value, plus 3, comes to exactly 0. What is the hub's regional figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_002136: A brick plant meters its ram drive through a stroke, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 1 times t squared plus 1 times t. The pressed block's acceleration, in metres per second squared, equals the total accumulated between the 0th and the 3rd second. The block has a mass of 31 kg, and the plant's kiln stack is 25 m tall. Four rams work each press, and the press log then adds 7 N for the ejector spring. Five presses make up a bank, and the plant runs 10 identical banks. What total force do the plant's presses supply, in N?
w10_P4_002138: A shipyard slipway drives a cradle of mass 139 kg. The cradle's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is twice the sum of the two winch-dial readings, which are 8 and 1. Eight identical cradles are pulled on each slipway, and the yard has 7 slipways. The yard's gantry spans 60 m. The yard also runs a mirrored second site of identical layout, doubling the total. What total force do both sites supply, in kN?
